# Finance Billing Ops

Curated by Skill Harbor: an operator-grade billing workflow for founders who want the truth about their money, not generic payments advice. It starts from the freshest billing evidence (live data preferred; snapshots get an explicit timestamp), normalizes the picture (paid sales, active subscriptions, failed checkouts, refunds, disputes, duplicate subscriptions), then separates three things most tools conflate: the customer incident (duplicate checkout? broken self-serve? failed payment?), the product truth (does team billing really exist in code? are seats actually counted? does the site overstate current behavior?), and the recommendation. The discipline is evidence-first: never say "per seat" unless the entitlement path enforces it, never infer team billing from marketing language, never compare competitor pricing from memory when current evidence is available. Output follows a fixed shape: snapshot, customer impact, product truth, decision (refund, preserve, convert, no-op), and the exact product or backlog gap to build next. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: it references sibling ECC skills (customer-billing-ops, github-ops, verification-loop) for full depth on remediation and code inspection; standalone it works as a rigorous operator checklist, but pair it with those for the complete loop.
